Case_17010/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Computed tomography (CT) scan of the chest demonstrating enlarged mediastinal, supraclavicular, mesenteric, and retroperitoneal lymph nodes, the largest of which was 1.52 cm in diameter (red arrow).

description.short_caption: CT scan of the chest showing an enlarged mediastinal lymph node (red arrow).
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates an enlarged mediastinal lymph node, highlighted by a red arrow. The node measures 1.52 cm in diameter, as indicated on the image. Surrounding structures, including the lungs and vertebrae, are visible, with no obvious signs of additional abnormalities in this slice. The scan appears to be performed with contrast, enhancing the visibility of vascular and lymphatic structures.
visible_findings: red arrow marking the lymph node

Case_17010/figure2.jpg.source_caption: A Diff-Quik stained specimen from a right supraclavicular lymph node core biopsy at 40X magnification reveals macrophages with numerous small (3-4 microns) intracytoplasmic yeast forms consistent with histoplasmosis (red arrow).

description.short_caption: Diff-Quik stain of lymph node biopsy shows macrophages with intracytoplasmic yeast forms.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Diff-Quik stained specimen from a right supraclavicular lymph node core biopsy at 40X magnification. Numerous macrophages are visible, containing small (3-4 microns) round to oval yeast forms within their cytoplasm. The yeast forms are highlighted by a red arrow, and their size and morphology are consistent with histoplasmosis. The background contains scattered lymphocytes and other inflammatory cells.
visible_findings: small (3-4 microns) round to oval yeast forms

Case_17010/figure3.jpg.source_caption: H&E stain of the right supraclavicular lymph node core biopsy demonstrating granulomatous inflammation (red arrow) and giant cells (blue arrow). (40x)

description.short_caption: H&E stain showing granulomatous inflammation and multinucleated giant cells in a lymph node biopsy (40x).
description.detailed_description: This is an H&E-stained histopathology slide of a right supraclavicular lymph node core biopsy at 40x magnification. The image demonstrates granulomatous inflammation, indicated by the red arrow, characterized by clusters of epithelioid histiocytes. The blue arrow highlights multinucleated giant cells, which are a hallmark of granulomatous processes. The background shows a mix of inflammatory cells and fibrotic tissue.
